rules.title: Invisible characters inside a word
rules.description: Characters that do not print sit between the letters of a word, so the word reads normally but does not match as text - a usual attempt to bypass static regex checks.

judge.instructions: Lower when the file is in a language that uses that script or is a test fixture for such text. One altered word in English prose keeps the severity.

rules.title: Look-alike characters inside a word
rules.description: Letters of another script that print like Latin letters sit inside a word next to Latin letters - a usual attempt to bypass static regex checks.

judge.instructions: Lower when the file is in a language that uses that script or is a test fixture for such text. One altered word in English prose keeps the severity.

decision.subject: lines
decision.question: The marked line holds a word that mixes Latin letters with letters of another script that print like Latin letters. The subject shows the word with those letters as code points, then the word as it reads. Why is the word written this way?

options.notation: the other letter is a symbol with its own meaning: a mathematical or physical quantity, a unit, a phonetic sign or a variable name.
options.other-language: the lines are text in a language that uses the other script, or text damaged by a wrong encoding, and the Latin letters next to it are an escape sequence, markup, a product name or a unit.
options.disguised-word: the word reads as an ordinary English word, command, file name or host name, and nothing in the lines explains a letter of another script inside it.
options.unknown: the lines do not show why the word is written this way.

rules.title: Link inside an HTML comment
rules.description: A Markdown file holds a URL inside an HTML comment. The rendered page hides it from the person who reads the skill, and the agent reads it as plain text.

judge.instructions: Lower when the comment is a note for the author, a credit or a license, and no step sends the agent to the URL.
